fit: green-tea history and nonmotor symptom status in two PRKN Parkinson cases
assessment: Table 1 lists never versus quit in the green tea row and absent olfactory dysfunction in both. Brew, timing, symptom change and an exposure effect are unreported.

fit: intranasal white tea extract and functional odor tests in stressed mice
assessment: Buried-food retrieval and the other odor tests favored intranasal white tea extract relative to stressed controls. Figure 3 involves a different tea, route and model from brewed green tea and Parkinson disease.

fit: cumin extract and isolated glycoside with an unrelated drug in rats
assessment: Aqueous seed extract enhanced rifampicin exposure. The 35% maximum concentration and 53% area increase refer to isolated glycoside. No ground cumin or levodopa comparison or daily OFF outcome.

fit: cumin extract combined with glyburide in diabetic rats
assessment: The abstract reports differing glyburide pharmacokinetics across different doses with and without ethanolic extract. This gives no clinical levodopa or daily OFF estimate.

fit: five-ingredient extract cocktail and spatial attention in aged dogs
assessment: Variable-distance landmark errors favored the cocktail in 7 treated and 6 placebo dogs. Pepper was present as a standardized extract and the tested combination supplies no separate pepper estimate.
